features.feature: Warn-only PreToolUse(Bash) hook that detects CJK in git commit and lattice story-metadata commands
Hook prints warning to stderr and exits 0 (non-blocking; command still proceeds)
Hook must be generated as a managed asset via init-assets.ts and managed-assets.ts (not hand-written)
Diff/story-scoped CJK gate in lattice validate (review-preflight.ts) that hard-blocks REVIEW to TEST
CJK gate scoped to current story/branch diff only (commit subjects/bodies + author-controlled story metadata); never scans whole repo
Legacy Chinese files outside the current story diff must not be flagged (no retroactive flagging)
Shared core/cjk-detect.ts module reused by both the hook and the validate gate
Hook resilience: malformed/empty stdin or missing tool_input must not crash the hook; must exit 0
Unit tests for CJK detector: positive (Chinese detected), negative (ASCII/English not detected), and mixed range cases
Integration test: validate gate fails non-zero on a CJK fixture commit/metadata and passes English-only
Scope test: legacy/outside-story file is not flagged by the gate
Keep-in-sync test: the self-contained hook CJK range must match the shared core/cjk-detect.ts range
Phase 3 gate (english-open-source-surface-smoke): smoke test that fails on new Chinese text in active source AND active docs broadly (not limited to commits/story-metadata)
Phase 3 gate explicit allowlists: review document, generated translation manifests, legacy archive docs, and compatibility tests are allowlisted
Out of scope: retroactively translating existing files

openQuestions.q: The decisions spec (cli-engine-english-open-source-execution-plan.md Phase 3) commits to a gate that fails on new Chinese text in active source AND active docs broadly. The story description explicitly excludes scanning arbitrary code/doc files and limits coverage to commits + lattice story metadata only. Are these two in tension? Is this story implementing only a partial subset of Phase 3 (with the broader active-source-scan deferred to a later story), or does the story description intentionally supersede the Phase 3 spec scope?
openQuestions.evidence: Spec says: Phase 3 - Add A No-New-Chinese Gate: Add a smoke test that fails on new Chinese text in active source and active docs. Story description says: Out of scope: retroactively translating existing files, and scanning arbitrary code/doc files (coverage = commits + lattice story metadata).
openQuestions.resolution: No tension and no supersession. Phase 3 of the execution plan is ALREADY implemented as packages/main/src/tasks/english-open-source-surface-smoke.ts, which scans the active SOURCE surface (packages/main/src/**/*.ts) and active DOCS (README, guides, decisions/*.md) for CJK with an explicit allowlist. This story B-5f42 deliberately covers a DIFFERENT, non-overlapping surface that Phase 3 does not scan: git commit messages and lattice story metadata (process artifacts under .lattice/story/actives), which is exactly where the B-4fd3 violation occurred. The description exclusion of arbitrary code/doc files defers that surface to the existing Phase 3 gate, not to a future story. For consistency the new core/cjk-detect.ts uses the same CJK ranges (U+4E00-9FFF plus U+3400-4DBF) as english-open-source-surface-smoke.ts. Therefore the two are complementary guards on distinct surfaces, both forward-looking and scoped.
